question.text: Scenario: Sarvottam Fintech Ltd. (SFL), an unlisted fintech company, plans to launch its IPO. The company's financials for the last three years show: net tangible assets of Rs.5 crore, Rs.4.2 crore, and Rs.3.8 crore; average operating profit of Rs.17 crore (positive each year); and net worth of Rs.2 crore each year. The IPO is structured as a book building issue with a price band of Rs.280-Rs.320 per share. The total issue size is 50 lakh shares, comprising 35 lakh fresh issue shares and 15 lakh shares as Offer for Sale by the promoter, Harish Mehta. The issue receives the following subscription on closing day (T day): QIB category -- 1.5 crore shares bid (against 25 lakh shares reserved); NII category -- 60 lakh shares bid (against 7.5 lakh shares reserved); RII category -- 52.5 lakh shares bid (against 17.5 lakh shares reserved). The cut-off price is determined at Rs.310 per share. Pooja Sharma, a retail investor, applied for 200 shares at cut-off price through ASBA, with funds blocked in her SCSB account. Vikram Desai, the RTA officer, is coordinating the post-issue process. Question 1 of 5: Based on SFL's stated financials and assuming that monetary assets are not more than 50% of net tangible assets, is the company eligible for a standard IPO under SEBI ICDR Regulations?

answer.text: No, because the average operating profit is below Rs.20 crore
No, because the net worth of Rs.2 crore each year exceeds the permitted limit

Yes, assuming monetary assets are not more than 50% of net tangible assets, because net tangible assets are >= Rs.3 crore each year, average operating profit is >= Rs.15 crore, and net worth is >= Rs.1 crore each year
No, because an unlisted fintech company cannot make a public offer under SEBI regulations

explanation.text: The Logic: Checking each numerical threshold from page 84: net tangible assets are Rs.5 cr, Rs.4.2 cr and Rs.3.8 cr, all >= Rs.3 crore each year; average operating profit is Rs.17 crore, which is >= Rs.15 crore; net worth is Rs.2 crore each year, which is >= Rs.1 crore. Under the stated assumption that monetary assets are not more than 50% of net tangible assets, SFL meets the standard eligibility tests on these criteria. The Trap: The operating-profit threshold is Rs.15 crore, not Rs.20 crore, and there is no source-stated prohibition on fintech companies making public offers. Without the monetary-assets assumption, eligibility cannot be concluded from the stated facts alone. Note: Page 84 also lists a separate condition tied to a name change in the recent past; since the scenario does not state a name change, it is treated as not applicable here.
